newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BRAVES EDGE ASTROS TO WIN SIXTH STRAIGHT GAME.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BRAVES EDGE ASTROS TO WIN SIXTH STRAIGHT GAME.

text.p: Fred McGriff's bases-loaded walk in the bottom of the 12th inning forced home Jeff Blauser with the winning run as the Atlanta Braves edged the Houston Astros 4-3 for their sixth straight victory on Wednesday.
Alan Embree (1-0) worked a perfect 12th for the victory. Braves pitchers did not allow a hit over the final 6-1/3 innings.
"We had plenty of opportunities, that's a tough way to lose," said Astros first baseman Jeff Bagwell."

At Colorado, Ellis Burks homered twice and drove in three runs while Andres Galarraga and Dante Bichette also had three RBI apiece as the Colorado Rockies continued their offensive potency with a 13-4 rout of the Cincinnati Reds.
Quinton McCracken added a two-run double for Colorado, which has won six straight games since losing its first two games at Cincinnati.
Mark Thompson (2-0) picked up the win for the Rockies, giving up four runs and nine hits over 6-1/3 innings.
In Los Angeles, Mike Piazza singled home Brett Butler with one out in the bottom of the 14th inning, giving the Los Angeles Dodgers another marathon victory over the New York Mets 3-2.
Butler also scored the winning run in the Dodgers' 3-2, 15-inning victory on Tuesday.
Tom Candiotti (2-0), Los Angeles' sixth pitcher, worked a perfect 14th to get the win.
The loss spoiled a stellar effort by Mets' reliever Rick Reed, who allowed one hit over five innings with no walks and seven strikeouts.
In San Francisco, Kirk Rueter and two relievers combined on a five-hitter and Barry Bonds belted a two-run homer in the first inning as the San Francisco Giants blanked the Philadelphia Phillies 3-0.
Rueter (1-0) gave up four hits and no walks with four strikeouts over seven innings.
Bonds followed Jose Vizcaino's single in the first with his first homer of the year.
In San Diego, Esteban Loaiza allowed one run in 7 1/3 innings and had an RBI single in a two-run seventh as the Pittsburgh Pirates defeated the slumping San Diego Padres, 4-2.
Loaiza (1-0) scattered five hits while striking out four. John Ericks got the final three outs for his fourth save.
Kevin Elster hit a solo homer for the Pirates.
Tony Gwynn hit his first home run of the season, a two-run shot in the eighth, to account for San Diego's only runs.
